title: One turn through Deep Agents
example_input: Survey the utils package and the config loader in this repository, and summarize what each one does.
note: Representations below are simplified shapes of the real types at the pinned SHAs, not verbatim dumps.

modules.label: deepagents graph.py:989-1010 — the create_agent return, config stamped
langchain factory.py:1896-1926 — the factory stamps the same limit

steps.narrative: The application calls create_deep_agent with a LocalShellBackend rooted at the repository. Deep Agents resolves the model and its profile, assembles the middleware stack, compiles the general-purpose subagent, composes the base prompt — and returns LangChain's create_agent(...), with recursion_limit 9_999 and ls_integration: deepagents stamped onto the config. Nothing has run yet; what exists is a compiled LangGraph graph whose loop belongs to the dependencies.
steps.representation:
agent = create_deep_agent(model, backend=LocalShellBackend(root_dir=repo))
  stack := [Filesystem, SubAgent, Summarization,
            PatchToolCalls, (caching)]
  subagents compiled via create_agent(...)
  -> create_agent(...).with_config(
       recursion_limit=9_999,
       metadata={"ls_integration": "deepagents"})
steps.title: Construction: the stack is assembled, the loop is borrowed

steps.code: agent.invoke({messages}, config={configurable: {thread_id}}) — Pregel writes the input checkpoint
steps.narrative: The caller invokes the graph with the survey prompt on a thread. Pregel loads the thread's checkpoint (none yet), applies the input, and saves a checkpoint marked source: input. The first super-steps run the middleware state hooks in graph order — the before_agent nodes, where PatchToolCallsMiddleware's repair scan finds no dangling tool calls in a fresh history — then the before_model nodes. No model call has happened; the runtime has already checkpointed once.
steps.representation:
invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage(prompt)]},
       {"configurable": {"thread_id": "survey-1"}})
  -> checkpoint {source: "input"}
  -> super-step: before_agent nodes
       (PatchToolCalls repair scan)
  -> super-step: before_model nodes
steps.title: The input lands: an input checkpoint, then the before-hooks

steps.code: the factory chains wrap_model_call handlers; the system prompt is composed per call
steps.narrative: The model node builds its request: the system prompt composed for this call (base prompt plus profile suffix; no memory middleware in this assembly), the history, and the bound tools — the filesystem seven, the permissions-filtered execute, and task. The request travels the chained wrap_model_call handlers in stack order; summarization runs its trigger arithmetic against the reconstructed history and finds it far below the threshold, so no compaction event is recorded and the request passes through unchanged.
steps.representation:
ModelRequest(model, system_prompt, messages, tools)
  system_prompt = base + profile suffix   (per call)
wrap chain (stack order):
  filesystem -> subagent -> summarization -> ...
  summarization: price(history) << trigger
               -> no event; pass through
steps.title: Before the model: the prompt is composed, the wrappers are armed

steps.code: model_node: bind tools, invoke; the routing edge returns one Send per pending call

modules.label: langchain factory.py:2034-2043 — one Send per pending call

steps.narrative: At the end of the wrapper chain the model node's handler binds the tools and invokes the model. The reply carries two task calls and no direct file calls — the model delegates both halves of the survey. The routing edge inspects the reply: tool calls are pending, so instead of END it returns one Send per call, and Pregel prepares both as parallel tasks of the next super-step — one tools-node execution each, in the same step.
steps.representation:
reply = AIMessage(tool_calls=[
    task("survey the utils package..."),
    task("audit the config loader...")])
routing(reply) =
  [Send("tools", task_call_1),
   Send("tools", task_call_2)]   # parallel tasks
steps.title: The first model call: a reply full of delegations

steps.code: subagents.py — _build_state subtracts; subagent.invoke runs the nested graph
steps.narrative: Each Send task runs the task tool inside ToolNode, through the chained wrap_tool_call wrappers. SubAgentMiddleware builds the subagent's state by subtraction: the parent's state minus the curated exclusion set, with the message history replaced by a single HumanMessage carrying the task description. It then calls subagent.invoke synchronously — a complete nested run of the same machinery, with its own super-steps, on the caller's thread unless the subagent spec names its own checkpointer.
steps.representation:
per task call (inside the tools node):
  state = {k: v for k, v in parent.items()
           if k not in EXCLUDED_FROM_SUBAGENT}
  state["messages"] = [HumanMessage(task_text)]
  result = subagent.invoke(state)   # nested run
steps.title: Delegation, twice: state subtraction at the subgraph boundary

steps.code: ToolNode executes; FilesystemMiddleware resolves each call against the backend
steps.narrative: Inside each subagent, the same loop runs with a smaller stack. The models explore with ls, read_file, and grep; each call passes through ToolNode into FilesystemMiddleware, which resolves the backend from state and calls it — here LocalShellBackend's file operations against its jailed root. No execute call is made in this trace: the reads suffice, so the host-shell capability wired into this assembly is never exercised.
steps.representation:
subagent loop (smaller stack, no task tool):
  ls("/")  read_file("/pkg/...")  grep("...")
    -> ToolNode -> FilesystemMiddleware
       -> backend.ls / read / grep
          (root-jailed paths)
  execute: bound, never called in this trace
steps.title: Inside the subagents: tools fire, the backend answers

steps.code: subagents.py — one ToolMessage per task call; after_tick saves the checkpoint

modules.label: langgraph pregel/_loop.py:786 — checkpoint after the super-step

steps.narrative: Each nested run ends with a plain-text answer. _validate_and_prepare_state and the result extraction reduce each final state to exactly one ToolMessage on the parent's original task call — the structured response if one was produced, otherwise the last AI message's text. Both tasks' writes merge into the parent state in one super-step, and after_tick saves the checkpoint. The parent's next model request re-prices the history for summarization; two survey summaries do not move it anywhere near the trigger.
steps.representation:
result_1.result -> ToolMessage(task_call_1)
result_2.result -> ToolMessage(task_call_2)
  (structured_response, else last AIMessage text)
writes merge in one super-step
  -> checkpoint {source: "loop"}
parent history re-priced: still under trigger
steps.title: Results return; compaction stays out of the way

steps.code: factory.py — no tool calls routes to END; the final checkpoint closes the thread state

modules.label: langchain factory.py:2020-2022 — the classic exit condition

steps.narrative: The parent model reads the two ToolMessages and answers the survey directly, with no further tool calls. The routing edge takes the comment-named classic exit: no pending calls routes to END. The after_model and after_agent hook nodes run on the way out — nothing in this assembly changes anything there — the final checkpoint is written, and invoke returns the state. The whole turn consumed a handful of super-steps against the 9,999 ceiling, and not one of them was counted by any code in the deepagents package.
steps.representation:
reply = AIMessage(text) with tool_calls == []
routing(reply) -> END
  ("the classic exit condition")
after_model / after_agent nodes run
final checkpoint written
return {"messages": [...]}
steps.title: Exit: no tool calls is the whole condition
